mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment exceeding 7.5% indicates a weakening labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate above 4.5% and 12-month CPI inflation exceeding 2.0% signal aggressive monetary tightening amid persistent inflation, triggering equity sell-offs within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated housing demand (HOUST > 850.0) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in high housing demand regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 850.0.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that precedes higher corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth (quarterly) is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strengthening manufacturing output, which correlates with improved corporate profitability and positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Annualized employment growth below 0.5% (PAYEMS) signals a slowing labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS 12m % change is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent unemployment rises (>0.1pp) and weak employment growth (PAYEMS 12m % change < 0.5%) indicate labor market deterioration that depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.1pp in 1 month and PAYEMS 12m % change < 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition.
